title: Canonical usage telemetry views and Iceberg partitioning strategy for Console analytics
creator: Evan Park
description:
Problem: Console analytics currently relies on multiple ad-hoc event exports and overlap between sessionized invocation tables and raw event streams. This causes duplicate ETL logic, inconsistent tenant-level metrics, and slow ad-hoc queries for SLA/cost attributions.

Goal: Design and implement a canonical set of curated analytics tables stored in Iceberg with an explicit partitioning and compaction strategy to support fast slice-and-dice for the Console UI and downstream billing/alerting systems. Deliverables: 1) canonical wide event view (console_event_canonical) optimized for fast filter-by-tenant/date/route, 2) compact weekly tenant rollups and sessionized invocation table for SLO analysis, 3) managed Iceberg partitioning and compaction policy, 4) migration plan and backfill strategy with data correctness validation harness.
schema_summary: console_event_canonical: denormalized wide view. key fields: event_ts (timestamp), event_date (date), tenant_id, tenant_hash (32-bit), route_id, route_variant, user_id, session_id, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, model_version, invocation_id, ingestion_ts
session_stitch_fact: session_id, tenant_id, first_ts, last_ts, invocation_count, total_tokens, outcome_set (error/success), primary_route
tenant_week_rollup: tenant_id, iso_week, total_invocations, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, total_request_tokens, total_response_tokens, cost_estimate_cents
route_dim (SCD2): route_id, current_variant, owner_team, created_at, retired_at, route_tags
invocation_latency_histogram_mv: precomputed HDR buckets per route/tenant/day for fast percentile queries
partitioning_strategy: Table format: Apache Iceberg on GCP (Dataproc + Iceberg + BigQuery-compatible read via BigLake) or equivalent S3/Hive stack for on-prem installs
Primary partition keys: (event_date, tenant_hash_bucket) where tenant_hash_bucket = sha256(tenant_id) mod 256 to avoid small-tenant skew
Secondary micro-partitions: hour_of_day for hot query locality (compact files per hour per tenant bucket)
Hidden sort order (Z-order-like): (tenant_id, route_id, event_ts) for fast equality+range scans
Compaction cadence: micro-commit window = 5min, hourly compaction for small files, daily major compaction with rewrite planning using Iceberg rewrite-manifests
Retention and TTL: raw event snapshot retention = 90 days; curated weekly rollups retained for 3 years; cost-sensitive tenants can opt-in for longer retention
ingestion_flow: Source: event bus (Kafka topic: console-invocations-v2) and fallback S3 batched exports
Stream processor: Spark Structured Streaming job (Dataproc Serverless) with exactly-once sinks to Iceberg using checkpointed write paths
Late data handling: watermark = 24 hours; late events routed to a 'late_events' Iceberg partition and reprocessed daily into canonical view
Enrichment: join with route_dim SCD2 table (upserted via CDC job) and tenant_metadata service cache (TTL 5m) to fill owner_team and billing_tier
Validation: checksum diff vs parallel snapshot job for first 7 days after rollout
Backfill: incremental backfill via time-windowed Spark jobs using snapshot isolation and idempotent writes (invocation_id primary key)
consistency_and_evolution: SCD2 pattern for route_dim to preserve historical mappings needed for retrospective SLA costing
Schema evolution: use Iceberg's schema-change APIs for safe adds/removals; maintain a canonical column list used by Console UI queries
Column-level lineage tags stored as table properties for ownership and privacy classification
Audit columns: ingested_by_job, source_offset, source_partition to assist incident triage
query_patterns_and_optimizations: Common Console queries: filter by tenant/date range/route, compute latency percentiles, cost by model_version, session funnels
Precomputed rollups: tenant_day and tenant_week tables for cost dashboards to avoid scanning canonical event table
Adaptive materialized views: hour-level latency sketches maintained via scheduled jobs for high-cardinality slices
Join strategy: prefer broadcast join for small route_dim and tenant metadata; use shuffle-repartition for heavy joins with session_stitch_fact
Cost control: limit broad scans with per-query quota and automated fallback to rollups if estimated bytes scanned exceed threshold
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for schema migrations and Iceberg partition predicates
Integration tests: run streaming job against a synthetic dataset in staging, compare aggregates to golden outputs (p50/p95 counts, invocation sums)
Data correctness harness: nightly DAG that calculates row-count deltas and token-sum diffs between source snapshots and canonical view
Performance testing: run TPC-like slices that mimic Console UI queries and record 95th latency under target cluster sizes
updates: 2026-02-20: Created ticket and drafted initial goals after sync with PM/Console Analytics team.
2026-02-25: Spike complete — validated Iceberg write throughput ~12k rows/sec per worker; candidate partitioning chosen (tenant_hash + event_date).
2026-03-01: Prototype streaming job pushed to staging, PR opened (observability#842). Initial end-to-end ingest validated for low-volume tenants.
2026-03-05: PM review: asked for explicit cost-estimation model per tenant and an opt-in long-retention flag. Added to requirements.
2026-03-08: Design review with infra: added hidden sort order and hourly compaction to reduce small-file overhead. Estimate revised to 5 points.
2026-03-10: Began implementing tenant_week_rollup materialization job and a lightweight validation harness.
